solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dabbler in potions maybe St Michael converted

indicators.note: to convert something is to change its form, so the letters of the saint's name are rearranged

explanation.surface: A saint has been turned into a dabbler in magic potions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' looks like a religious conversion, apt beside a saint, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Medieval practitioners trying to turn base metal into gold also brewed elixirs, so a potion-dabbler is an example, signalled by 'maybe'.

clue.text: A desire that's often unexpressed in Bow

definitions.text: A desire that's often unexpressed in Bow

parts.note: an itch is a craving or desire

explanation.surface: A longing that people in East London keep to themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: Bow is in London's Cockney East End, where the H sound is famously dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of the letter H, which Cockneys habitually leave unpronounced.

clue.text: Sycophant needing queen to support slow progress

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece goes underneath, after the other

parts.note: to crawl is to make slow progress
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A toady needs the queen to back his slow advance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to support' puts ER below CRAWL.
explanation.definitionFit: A fawning toady who grovels to superiors is an obsequious flatterer.

clue.text: Old job description

parts.note: ex means former or old
a position is a job

explanation.surface: A description of a former role.
explanation.definitionFit: A detailed setting out of ideas or facts is an explanation or account.

clue.text: Banker in south of France upset

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: sud is French for south

explanation.surface: A banker in the South of France is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, which has banks; here the great river of Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks, so crosswords call one a banker; this one flows through Pakistan.

clue.text: Clement worried by tendency to blow top

parts.note: a temper is a tendency to lose one's cool
ate, as in 'what's eating you', means worried

explanation.surface: Clement was bothered by his inclination to explode with rage.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement looks like a man's name; it is the adjective. ATE as 'worried' is from 'eaten up with worry'.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement weather is mild, as is a climate that is neither hot nor cold.

clue.text: Animal fats regularly consumed in risky venture

indicators.note: the regular letters are eaten up by the word for the venture, so they go inside it

parts.note: a bet is a wager, a venture with risk

indicators.note: taking every other letter of the word fats, here the second and fourth

explanation.surface: An animal's fat is eaten during some hazardous undertaking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the second and fourth letters of fats; 'consumed in' puts them inside the wager.
explanation.definitionFit: A creature, especially a large four-legged one, is commonly called a brute or creature of this kind.

clue.text: City in which Archimedes made his discovery?

definitions.meaning: a spa city in Somerset, England

definitions.text: in which Archimedes made his discovery?
definitions.meaning: Archimedes noticed water displacement while getting into his tub and cried Eureka

explanation.surface: Which city did Archimedes make his great find in?
explanation.definitionFit: The English spa town shares its name with the tub Archimedes sat in when he had his insight.

clue.text: A sailor caught in storm

indicators.note: to catch words is to hear them, so the phrase is taken by its sound

parts.note: a salt is an old sailor, as in 'an old salt'

explanation.surface: A seaman is trapped in a tempest at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like capture, beside 'in storm', but means heard. 'Storm' is the military sense, as in storming a castle.
explanation.definitionFit: To storm a position is to attack it violently, so the noun or verb matches a violent attack.

clue.text: Official more confident after March, for the most part

indicators.note: the confident word comes after the marching word
most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: to march is to tread
surer means more confident

explanation.surface: An official has grown more confident since March.
explanation.walkthrough: March looks like the month; it is the verb. 'for the most part' cuts TREAD to TREA.
explanation.definitionFit: A club or society officer in charge of the money holds an official post.

clue.text: Caught deputy to some extent on the retreat

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the combined letters are read in reverse

parts.note: in part, partly

explanation.surface: A deputy was partly caught while running away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the retreat' reverses DEPPART as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: Something snared or cornered with no way out has been caught.

clue.text: Painter harboured by diplomat is secure

indicators.note: something harboured is sheltered within, so the name sits inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: An artist is given safe refuge by a diplomat.
explanation.walkthrough: The name runs across diploMAT IS SEcure.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Matisse was a French artist, a leader of Fauvism, known for bold colour.

clue.text: She flirts outrageously with a relation

indicators.note: behaving outrageously means acting wildly, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A woman flirts shamelessly with some relative of hers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' shuffles SHEFLIRTSA; 'with' just joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A sibling sharing only one parent is a family member, a kind of relative.

clue.text: Swear changing leader will bring this trouble

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is swapped for a different one

parts.note: to cuss is to curse or swear

explanation.surface: Bad language will only cause more bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing leader' replaces the C of CUSS with F.
explanation.definitionFit: Bother or commotion over something, as in making a to-do, is a synonym for trouble.

clue.text: Drink lots of wine and go to bed

definitions.meaning: sack is an old name for a dry white wine, so the phrase is read as going hard at it, like hitting the bottle
an idiom for retiring for the night

explanation.surface: Drink heavily, then retire for the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Sack is a sherry-like wine, so hitting it means drinking hard; the idiom means retiring to sleep.

clue.text: Expression of doubt in Cambridge University? Goodness!

indicators.note: the hesitation sound is placed inside the university's initials

parts.note: MIT, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology, is in Cambridge, Massachusetts
er is a hesitant noise expressing uncertainty

explanation.surface: Someone at Cambridge voices doubts and exclaims in surprise.
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge suggests the English university, but the ? hints at Cambridge, Massachusetts, home of MIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodness can mean worth or virtue, the quality of deserving praise.

clue.text: Small stream from which duck might emerge?

parts.note: micro means very small
a wave is a flow or surge, as in a stream of people

explanation.surface: A little brook from which a duck might pop out.
explanation.walkthrough: The stream and duck paint a pond, but the duck is a cooked one in the kitchen.
explanation.definitionFit: A kitchen oven that heats food quickly could produce a reheated duck dinner.

clue.text: One armed boy and I feeding creature of the swamps

indicators.note: the boy and I are fed into the reptile, so they go inside it

parts.note: gator is short for alligator, a swamp reptile
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy and I are giving food to an alligator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feeding' puts LADI inside GATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman arena fighter carried weapons, so he was a person bearing arms.

clue.text: Fish brought to bank is crowned as winner

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish
a fish hauled onto the bank has been landed

explanation.surface: An angler's fish brought ashore is hailed as the prize catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A victor was traditionally decked with a wreath of flowers or leaves on the head.

clue.text: Open area where classes can absorb corporal?

indicators.note: the classes take in the soldier, so his letters go inside

parts.note: a course is a series of classes
a corporal is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A space where lessons can take in an army corporal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corporal' with a question mark looks like corporal punishment in class, but it is the soldier's rank; 'can absorb' puts him inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A large open space in a station or airport where crowds gather is called this.

clue.text: Daughter raging about a stingy customer

indicators.note: about as in round about, so the letters are turned around into another order

explanation.surface: A daughter rages about a skinflint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' shuffles RAGING; D, though first in the clue, goes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A miserly person who hates spending is a stingy character, 'customer' meaning a type of person.

clue.text: Spring, time for Charlie to become thinner?

indicators.note: one letter stands in place of the other, swapped in

parts.note: a caper is a playful leap or spring
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Spring is the season when Charlie should slim down.
explanation.walkthrough: Spring looks like the season; it is a leap. 'time for Charlie' puts T in place of C.
explanation.definitionFit: To narrow gradually toward one end, like a candle or a spire, is to grow slimmer.

clue.text: Bishop at university recalled good Polish food

indicators.note: called back, so these letters are read backwards

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
being up means in residence at university
to rub is to polish

explanation.surface: A bishop at college remembers some good Polish cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish looks like the nationality; it is the verb. 'recalled' turns BUP round.
explanation.definitionFit: Simple meals served in a British bar or tavern are a kind of food.

clue.text: Bloody good going back for a binge!

indicators.note: the letter for good travels back to the rear of the word

parts.note: gory means bloody

explanation.surface: A violent good time is had at a drunken spree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going back' sends the G of GORY to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild party of excessive indulgence, in drink or anything else, is a bout of overindulgence.

clue.text: Airline gossip about what you might need in duty free?

definitions.text: what you might need in duty free?

parts.note: an airline is an air carrier

indicators.note: turned about, the chatter word reads backwards

parts.note: gab means chatter or gossip

explanation.surface: Airline staff talk about what shoppers need at the airport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses GAB.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoppers in airport stores need a plastic sack with handles to carry purchases.

clue.text: Teacher's pet? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of it, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a rabbit is a common pet

explanation.surface: Is this the teacher's pet? Not exactly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teacher's pet' reads as a favourite pupil; split it, and the 's is just 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jewish scholar and religious leader is a teacher of the law.

clue.text: Spirit a German, say, knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back as in drunk down, but here meaning turned backwards

parts.note: ein is German for a
eg, for example, is signalled by say

explanation.surface: A German knocks back some spirits, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' reverses EINEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A jinn released from a lamp to grant wishes is a supernatural being.

clue.text: Grow stern

definitions.meaning: to raise or bring up, as plants or children
the back part, as of a ship

explanation.surface: Become strict.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise crops or animals means to cultivate them; the back end of anything is its tail end.

clue.text: A nurse holding article up

indicators.note: the nursing word holds the article inside it

parts.note: to tend is to nurse or care for
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A nurse lifts some item up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a direction but is the definition, as in 'time is up'.
explanation.definitionFit: When time is up, it is finished or over, which the phrase also means.

clue.text: I nab RAF suspect, a foreigner

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or unreliable, signalling a rearrangement of the letters

explanation.surface: Someone catches an RAF man under suspicion of being a foreign agent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' shuffles INABRAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Biafra, the breakaway state in eastern Nigeria of 1967-70, is a person from abroad.

clue.text: Big joiner losing weight

indicators.note: the joiner loses a letter, which is removed

parts.note: a welder joins metal parts

explanation.surface: A large joiner is shedding weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, but here it is someone who joins metal.
explanation.definitionFit: An older sibling is the big brother or sister, so senior and grown up.

clue.text: Wild lark in bed going down OK?

indicators.note: wild means unruly, so these letters run riot into a new order

explanation.surface: Is a wild romp in bed acceptable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' shuffles LARKINBED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fit to swallow is fine when it slips down the throat.
